processing: A baked (hongqing) green tea: as with other baked greens, the leaf is fixed, rolled and dried with baking heat rather than panning.
harvest_season: Spring tea is made in March and April, within a growing season that runs from March to September.
appearance_dry: Plump leaf of a moist green, with obvious down.
appearance_wet: As is usual for a downy baked green, plump soft shoots of a fresh green.
taste_profile: Fresh and brisk with a sweet return on the finish.

brewing.notes: General advice for downy baked greens: water below the boil, with some haze from the hairs being normal.

vintage_note: Buy the current spring tea, from March and April; as is usual for baked green tea, it is at its best within the year. It is a protected geographical indication product, and Wuxiang is the farm's registered brand.
description:
Yanxishan Baimao Jian comes from Yanxi Mountain in Lechang, northern Guangdong, on slopes at 400 to 800 metres. Of the white-haired teas of this corner of the province, it is the one with a named farm and a clear modern story.

It is a baked green tea, with plump, glossy green leaf and visible down.

The cup is a bright tender green, fresh and brisk with a sweet finish. Keep the water under the boil, and do not worry about a slight haze, because that is simply the down coming off.

It is a protected geographical indication tea, and the Wuxiang brand is the one to know. Ask for this year's spring lot.
history:
Local accounts claim more than 1,200 years of tea growing here and a visit by Lu Yu to look at Lechang's white-haired tea; both are local tradition rather than firm record.

The firmer history is modern. In 1956 the Yanxishan tea farm was founded on reclaimed land at the direction of Tao Zhu. The Wuxiang trademark was registered in 1993, and Guangdong brand honours followed in 2006 and 2007.
